title: Software Engineer Summer Intern, AI Compute Libraries & Performance 2027
description: <p><strong>Location:</strong> Bristol, UK<br><strong>Salary: </strong>£2500 per month<br><strong>Start date: </strong>June 2027<br><strong>Application deadline</strong>: Midnight, 29th November 2026 <br><em>We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.</em></p> <h3>The Internship Programme at Graphcore</h3> <p>Explore a career at Graphcore through a 12-week summer internship, gaining hands-on experience on real projects. You’ll bring fresh ideas, put your learning into practice and help shape what we’re creating. Along the way, you’ll tackle challenging problems with a team who welcome your questions and support you as you build your skills and confidence.</p> <h3>What you’ll work on</h3> <p>Use your programming skills and curiosity to help AI models run efficiently on next-generation Graphcore hardware. </p> <p>In AI Compute Libraries & Performance, you’ll contribute to C++ libraries and compute kernels for machine learning workloads. Your work will include: </p> <ul> <li><strong>Developing compute kernels:</strong> Implement and improve operations such as matrix multiplication (GEMM), convolutions, reductions, elementwise operations and fused kernels that combine multiple operations. </li> <li><strong>Understanding and improving performance:</strong> Use profiling and microbenchmarks to measure execution speed and investigate how threading, cache locality, memory layout and kernel launch efficiency affect performance. </li> <li><strong>Checking correctness and reliability:</strong> Build regression tests and numerical checks, investigate issues and improve the quality of the libraries our customers use. </li> </ul> <p>Through these projects, you’ll develop practical experience connecting numerical computing with how code runs on hardware, helping deliver software that is fast, accurate and reliable. </p> <h3>Your team and support</h3> <p>You’ll join a team building high-performance compute libraries that help customers get more from Graphcore hardware. Our work brings together machine learning, numerical computing and accelerator performance, with colleagues sharing their expertise to solve engineering problems.</p> <p><span data-contrast="none">You’ll contribute to clearly scoped projects and build your skills with guidance from engineers working in performance and low-level software. Together, we use profiling, experiments and technical reviews to compare approaches, understand trade-offs and improve our solutions.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">Your buddy will help you settle in, get familiar with our tools and ways of working, and find the right people to ask. Your manager will meet with you regularly to agree goals, offer feedback and discuss your development, including time for learning.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="none">We welcome different perspectives and make space for everyone to contribute. Questions, alternative approaches and requests for help are part of how we work. As you take on more responsibility, your colleagues will help you work through challenges, and your ideas will be listened to and discussed respectfully.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559738":240,"335559739":240,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <h3>How you’ll learn and grow</h3> <p>Over the 12 weeks, you’ll build performance engineering skills through hands-on work on compute kernels, benchmarks and tests.<span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Profiling and experiments will help you understand where time is spent and how changes to code and data layout affect performance. Numerical validation and regression testing will show you how to check that an optimisation preserves correct results and continues to work as software changes.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Working with specialists and discussing technical trade-offs will help you develop your engineering judgement, explain your findings and connect mathematical operations to efficient implementations on hardware.</span></p> <h3>What we're looking for</h3> <ul> <li>Currently studying towards a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field</li> <li>Experience with C or C++11, plus familiarity with Python or scripting tools for automation and testing</li> <li>An understanding of linear algebra, numerical methods or scientific computing</li> <li>Problem-solving skills and collaborative approach to unfamiliar technical challenges</li> </ul> <p>Previous industry experience is not required. Tell us what you built or investigated through coursework, personal or team projects or other relevant experience, how you approached it and what you learned.</p> <p>Coursework or experience with machine learning frameworks, parallel programming, code optimisation, maths libraries or performance analysis would be useful. These are additional strengths, rather than essential requirements.</p> <h3>Benefits</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Flexible working:</strong> Find a balance between your internship and life outside work</li> <li><strong>5 days of annual leave:</strong> Take time to rest and recharge during your 12-week internship</li> <li><strong>Life in the office:</strong> Get to know your colleagues in spaces designed for collaboration, with free food, a great selection of ice cream and an on-site barista</li> <li><strong>Learning and development:</strong> Build your skills and explore your interests with access to O’Reilly, our online learning platform</li> </ul> <p>We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.</p> <p>We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.</p> <h3>Sponsorship</h3> <p>Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.</p> <h3>Introduction to Graphcore</h3> <p>At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: From semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier.<br>Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.</p> <h3>How to apply and what to expect </h3> <p>To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.</p> <p>Curious about where your skills could take you? <strong>Apply for a summer internship at Graphcore and help us build what comes next.</strong></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Graduate Software Engineer, System Software QA 2027
description: <p><strong>Location:</strong> Bristol or Cambridge, UK <br><strong>Start date: </strong>September 2027<br><strong>Application deadline</strong>: Midnight, 29th November 2026 <br><em>We encourage you to apply early, as we may close applications before the advertised deadline.</em></p> <h3>The Graduate Programme at Graphcore</h3> <p>Join Graphcore in a permanent role and start your career with two years of hands-on learning. From day one, you’ll be trusted to take ownership, share your ideas and help shape what we’re creating. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.</p> <p><iframe style="display: table; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/sUqy-WuXPsE" width="560" height="314"></iframe></p> <h3>What you’ll work on</h3> <p>Put your programming and Linux skills to work on the software that helps Graphcore’s AI systems run reliably.</p> <p>As a Graduate Software Engineer in System Software Quality Assurance (QA), you’ll help validate low-level firmware, Linux kernel drivers and platform tools. You’ll design and develop tests, investigate issues and give development teams clear feedback on software quality.</p> <p>You’ll also maintain and improve continuous integration pipelines across different platforms. Working closely with System Software development teams, you’ll help strengthen test-driven development and solve practical engineering problems that matter to customers.</p> <h3>Your team and support</h3> <p>You will be working closely with a team of passionate engineers who will help you each step of the way. You’ll tackle challenging problems alongside a team who support your development and are as excited about your success as you are.</p> <p><iframe style="display: table; margin-left: auto; margin-right: auto;" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/sUqy-WuXPsE" width="560" height="314"></iframe> </p> <h3>What you’ll work on</h3> <p>Put your technical foundations to work on the infrastructure solutions that keeps Graphcore’s engineering teams connected, productive and secure. As a Graduate IS Engineer, you’ll support infrastructure operations, investigate technical issues and contribute to projects that improve reliability, performance and security. Your work will span servers, storage, networking, cloud platforms, automation and monitoring. You’ll learn how these systems support AI engineering at scale, building practical experience with Linux, Windows, scripting and infrastructure as code. It’s a chance to see how the technology behind an engineering organisation works and help make it better.</p> <h3>Your team and support</h3> <p>The Infrastructure Solutions team designs, builds and supports the IT environments that help Graphcore engineers work at scale. The team spans on-premise infrastructure, cloud, networking, automation and security. You’ll learn from experienced engineers through hands-on problem solving, planned projects and technical discussions. You’ll take ownership of useful, well-scoped work early, with support as you build your knowledge and confidence.</p> <p>You’ll gain hands-on experience as you rotate through our IS teams, including Cloud and Application Security, Cybersecurity Operations, Networking, Data Centre Operations and more. Along the way, Martinus and Peter will provide mentoring and support to help you build your skills, grow your confidence and take the next steps in your career.</p> <p>We use evidence, service impact and practical trade-offs to guide our decisions. You’ll be encouraged to ask questions, challenge existing approaches and share ideas for making things better. Take responsibility for your work and speak up when you spot a problem or need support.</p> <h3>How you’ll learn and grow</h3> <p>During the two-year programme, you’ll build infrastructure skills by working on real operational issues and improvement projects. Investigating technical issues will help you develop a methodical approach to problem solving and understand how servers, storage, networks and cloud services fit together. Work on scripting, automation and infrastructure as code will give you practical ways to improve how infrastructure is managed. Working alongside experienced engineers will help you weigh up reliability, performance and security, explain your approach and understand how infrastructure decisions affect the teams who depend on these services.</p> <h3>What we're looking for</h3> <ul> <li>Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Computer Science, Maths, Machine Learning, Data Science or a related field</li> <li>Familiarity with Linux or Windows server environments</li> <li>An understanding of networking fundamentals such as TCP/IP, DNS, routing or firewalls</li> <li>Introductory scripting experience with Python, Bash or PowerShell</li> </ul> <p>Bring an interest in infrastructure, cloud technologies, systems engineering or platform operations, and motivation to learn through practical problem solving. You can demonstrate these skills through coursework, a dissertation, personal or team projects, internships, hobbies or other relevant experience. Tell us what you built or investigated, how you approached it and what you learned.</p> <h3>Benefits</h3> <ul> <li>Flexible working: Balance your work and personal life with greater flexibility</li> <li>Retirement planning support: Up to 5% matched pension</li> <li>Phantom equity: Share in Graphcore’s success</li> <li>Workplace experience: Enjoy thoughtfully designed office spaces for collaboration, with free food and an on-site barista to support your day</li> <li>Peace of mind protection: Income protection and life assurance to provide financial security for you and your loved ones</li> <li>Electric Vehicle Scheme: Choose an electric vehicle and lease it through salary sacrifice</li> <li>Flexible benefits: Tailor your benefits package with a choice of additional options, including private medical insurance and dental cover</li> <li>Optional benefits: Dental cover, health cash plan, private medical insurance, cycle to work scheme, give as you earn</li> </ul> <p>We welcome people from all backgrounds and experiences and are committed to building an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.<br><br>We’re an equal opportunity employer and recognise that everyone brings different strengths and perspectives. If you need any adjustments during the interview process, just let us know - we’re happy to support you.</p> <h3>Sponsorship</h3> <p>Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK for the full duration of the programme, without requiring visa sponsorship. We are unable to sponsor work visas for our Early Careers opportunities.</p> <h3>Introduction to Graphcore</h3> <p>At Graphcore, we’re building next generation AI compute: from semiconductors and software to systems at datacenter scale. We are proud to be owned by SoftBank Group and work with other companies in the SoftBank family to deliver AI compute to customers working at the AI frontier. Starting your career here means working alongside people with different backgrounds and expertise, from AI researchers to chip designers and software engineers. You’ll learn from each other, bring fresh ideas and help solve challenging problems together.</p> <h3>How to apply and what to expect </h3> <p>To apply, answer the application questions below and upload your CV and cover letter. We’ll let you know the outcome of your application by early December at the latest. If successful, you’ll be invited to complete a technical assessment. Candidates who reach the final stage will then be invited to attend in-person assessments in early spring.</p> <p><em><strong>Ready to put your learning into practice? Start your career in a permanent IT Infrastructure Engineer role, with two years of hands-on learning through the Graphcore Graduate Programme. Apply now and help shape what comes next.</strong></em></p> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect
description: <p>A newly created role to help Databricks create new product categories. As Databricks accelerates its most strategic products, we are investing ahead of the curve in the partner ecosystem that helps our customers adopt them, and we are building a new specialisation function to lead that effort. You will pioneer it across EMEA.</p> <p>Reporting to: Director, Partner Field Engineering (EMEA).</p> <p>As the Senior Product Specialist Partner Solutions Architect, you own how our leading System Integrator partners develop deep, market-leading expertise in Databricks' priority products:</p> <ul> <li><strong>OLTP/Postgres (Lakebase):</strong> Databricks' fully managed, Postgres-compatible operational (OLTP) database for intelligent applications</li> <li><strong>Product AI (Genie):</strong> Databricks' natural-language analytics experience, letting anyone ask questions of governed data conversationally</li> <li><strong>AI Router & Governance (Unity Gateway):</strong> Databricks' governed gateway for securely managing, monitoring and routing access to AI and large language model endpoints</li> <li><strong>Migrations & Modernisation:</strong> moving legacy data warehouses and platforms onto the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform</li> <li><strong>Turn-key Solutions:</strong> Cybersecurity (Lakewatch) and CDP (CustomerLake) with more to come</li> </ul> <p>Your mandate is to take our leading partners to the highest tier of Centre-of-Excellence product specialisation on these products, and to turn them into independent, market-leading extensions of the Databricks field. Working hand in hand with our EMEA Product Specialist team, you will carry both the deep technical narrative and the business-value and go-to-market narrative that get these products positioned, adopted and scaled through the partner channel. This is a builder's role: you will design the blueprint for a partner product-specialist function that Databricks scales globally, starting in EMEA.</p> <h2><strong>What we are trying to achieve</strong></h2> <p>Databricks' priority products are seeing strong momentum across EMEA. Lakebase is one of the fastest-growing additions to our platform, Unity Gateway is newly generally available, and AI/BI + Genie are changing how customers work with their data. As adoption accelerates, our partners are central to helping customers realise value quickly and at scale. Deepening partner expertise in these products is one of the most powerful levers we have to accelerate customer time-to-value, and this role exists to build that capability deliberately and ahead of demand, so our partners lead the market.</p> <h2><strong>What the role owns</strong></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Building the partner specialist community (the day-to-day).</strong> Select, enable and certify leading EMEA partners to the highest tier of product specialisation, running the enablement engine end to end: partner selection, technical upskilling to expert depth, certification and first joint customer wins.</li> <li><strong>Partnering with our Product Specialist team.</strong> Act as the partner-side counterpart to Databricks' EMEA Product Specialists, bringing the latest product expertise to partners, connecting partner enablement to live customer opportunities, and channelling partner and customer adoption insight back to our product organisation.</li> <li><strong>Scaling specialist capacity through partners.</strong> Grow models where specialised partners bring product-specialist capacity to joint customers, so expertise scales across the ecosystem.</li> <li><strong>Launch-partner motions.</strong> Position specialised partners as launch partners for major product releases, signalling ecosystem trust and accelerating go-to-market at each milestone.</li> <li><strong>Thought leadership and the business-value narrative.</strong> Author the "better-together" technical and commercial story for these products in the partner channel: reference architectures, positioning, partner offers and value framing that let partners sell and deliver independently. Be a visible voice for partner product specialisation, internally and externally.</li> <li><strong>Building the function.</strong> Define the operating model, the specialisation and certification criteria, the partner selection bar and the cadence, and create the template Databricks adopts to scale this function worldwide.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>The impact you will have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Accelerate customer adoption and time-to-value on Databricks' priority products by putting genuine product depth into the partner channel.</li> <li>Grow partner-led momentum behind our fastest-growing products, building partner capability ahead of the demand curve.</li> <li>Elevate leading EMEA System Integrators to full independence on the priority products, so they operate as market leaders and true extensions of the Databricks field.</li> <li>Establish a repeatable, globally scalable partner product-specialist function, proven in EMEA and exported across Databricks.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What we look for</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Extensive hands-on experience with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, with genuine depth in at least two of the priority products above and the ability to get to depth quickly on the rest. This is a senior role for an established Databricks expert.</li> <li>Proven ability to build partner or field capability at scale: enablement, certification and community-building that turns others into independent experts.</li> <li>Strong business-value and go-to-market instinct: able to translate technical depth into commercial positioning and partner-led market impact, and to engage partner and customer organisations at senior-executive level.</li> <li>Demonstrated thought leadership: authoring technical and business content (reference architectures, solution guides, positioning, playbooks) and presenting complex products credibly to technical and executive audiences.</li> <li>At least 5 years of technical pre-sales or sales-methodology experience in a consumption business model, and experience designing and delivering end-to-end data, warehousing and AI architectures.</li> <li>Coding experience in a core language (Python, SQL, Java or Scala) and hands-on experience building data applications or AI agents.</li> <li>The maturity to build a new function from the ground up: defining the operating model, standards and cadence, and managing multiple changing priorities across a partner ecosystem and internal teams.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have:</strong> System Integrator or consulting background; experience with transactional databases (e.g. PostgreSQL) and application development; experience with LLM gateways, AI governance or AI security; experience running partner specialisation, certification or champion programmes; additional European languages.</p> <p>The role requires up to 40% travel across EMEA, to partner sites, Databricks offices and key industry events.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>About Databricks</strong></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, sans-serif;">Databricks is the Data and AI company. More than 20,000 organizations worldwide — including adidas, AT&T, Bayer, Block, Mastercard, Rivian, Unilever, and 70% of the Fortune 500 — rely on the Databricks Data + AI Platform to build and scale data and AI apps, analytics and agents. Headquartered in San Francisco with 30+ offices around the globe, Databricks offers a unified platform that includes Genie, Lakebase, Agent Bricks, Lakeflow, Lakehouse, and Unity Catalog. title: Staff Product Manager, Generative AI Platform
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Join us in our mission to transform the way people shop and eat. DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt now operate as one global company. Behind the AI experiences millions of people use every day, from shopping assistants to customer support agents, sits one shared Generative AI platform. Our team builds it. We're looking for a Staff Product Manager in London to own major parts of that platform. Your customers are the engineers and ML researchers across all three brands who build AI products and agents. You'll work with engineering and product leaders in Europe and the US, and your decisions will shape how AI gets built across every market we operate in. What You'll Be Doing Set the strategy and roadmap for core parts of our GenAI platform: model access and routing, agent infrastructure, and evaluation and observability. Build one platform for three brands. Spot the patterns across Deliveroo, Wolt and DoorDash teams and turn them into shared building blocks, so a capability built once reaches every market. Shape our model portfolio across frontier and open-weight models. Decide where we build, buy or partner in an ecosystem that changes month to month. Make agents production-ready. Give teams safe access to company knowledge, tools and systems, with the quality, latency and cost controls needed to run agents at scale. Own the evaluation strategy so teams can prove quality before launch and keep improving it after. Stay close to your customers. Work with the teams shipping AI experiences, measure adoption and time-to-production, and let real production use drive the roadmap. Lead at a senior level, presenting to senior technical leadership and influence strategy beyond your own roadmap. What You'll Need to Thrive Our ideal candidate brings deep expertise in some of these areas and curiosity to grow in others: Significant product management experience (typically 8+ years, or equivalent), including owning a technical platform, developer product, or ML or data infrastructure. Hands-on experience with LLM-based products or platforms in production, such as assistants, agents, evaluation or inference. GenAI platforms are a young field, so we care more about depth than years. A platform mindset. You notice the problem five teams keep solving and turn it into one capability everyone can use. The ability to go deep with engineers and ML researchers, then explain the trade-off in plain language to a senior leader. A track record of leading large, ambiguous areas on your own and aligning stakeholders across companies, countries and time zones. Comfort with regular overlap with US time zones, including some late-afternoon and evening calls. What Success Looks Like A team in any of our three brands can go from idea to a reliable AI product dramatically faster. That happens because the hard parts (models, inference, evaluation, tooling, observability, governance and agent infrastructure) are solved once at the platform layer and get better for everyone. Why Join Us? Real scale from day one. Your platform powers AI used by millions of consumers, merchants and couriers across three brands. Frontier work, real constraints. You'll work with the latest models and agent patterns, then make them reliable, affordable and compliant in production. Visible impact. title: 3D Computer Vision Research Engineer - World Map
description: About Niantic Spatial AI has learned from almost everything online, but it still struggles with the physical world, where 99.5% of economic activity happens. It doesn’t know where things are, how spaces fit together, or what changes over time. That’s one of the biggest unsolved problems in AI, and it’s the one we’re solving at Niantic Spatial. We build spatial AI models and services so people and machines can reason, learn and act safely in the physical world. We turn camera imagery, video, sensor data and archives into accurate, AI-readable representations of real places that robots can train in and machines can use to know exactly where they are. In physical AI, mistakes have real consequences. That’s why we build AI grounded in measured reality, not guesswork, so the people and machines relying on it can trust it to get things right. Our team built some of the world’s most widely used maps. Now we’re building something bigger: a living, measured record of the real world that machines can query, learn from and use to understand how places change over time. If you want to help AI understand the world we actually live in, come build with us. About the Role You'll help build the geometric foundation of the next-generation world map — joining our World Map Research Engineering team (Geospatial Alignment) as a Research Engineer or Senior Research Engineer. This is an end-to-end applied research role that spans from strong engineering and data-systems work to R&D in 3D deep learning, transformers, and foundation models. You'll develop new algorithms, produce the research data and evaluation assets needed to advance them, and engineer the resulting capabilities into dependable production systems. The World Map team works with heterogeneous captures from phones and handheld devices, aerial imagery, LiDAR, and 360 cameras, as well as external geographic and elevation data. The central challenge is to harmonize these data sources, quantify uncertainty, and maintain consistency as the map evolves. You'll work at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable engineering — developing new approaches to geospatial registration, correspondence, and geometric optimization, then productionizing these technologies to directly improve Niantic Spatial's world model. What You'll Do Geospatial Registration — Develop and advance algorithms for world-scale georeferencing and registration across imagery, 3D reconstructions, point clouds, and geographic reference data. 3D Geometry & Correspondence — Build and improve methods spanning multi-view geometry, SfM, SLAM, feature matching, learned correspondence, bundle adjustment, point-cloud registration, and ICP. Data & Evaluation — Create the data and evaluation flywheel for world-scale mapping — design and maintain large-scale datasets, pipelines, benchmarks, and evaluation methodologies that expose hard failure modes, accelerate research iteration, and support production. Learning-Based 3D Reasoning — Explore and develop learning-based approaches for geospatial understanding, combining transformers and 3D foundation models with geometric priors and uncertainty modeling. Production Robustness — Design robust solutions for challenging real-world conditions: sparse or noisy GPS, changing appearance, inconsistent reconstruction quality, large geographic extents, and imperfect reference maps. Cross-Functional Collaboration — Partner with leading researchers in visual localization, 3D computer vision, and mapping — as well as engineering and product teams — to identify high-impact problems and turn research breakthroughs into end-to-end production systems. Research Communication — Share results clearly through technical writing, design reviews, and internal presentations; contribute to publications and open research where appropriate. What You'll Bring Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Photogrammetry, or a closely related field — or equivalent research or industry experience. Strong grounding in 3D computer vision, machine learning, robotics, photogrammetry, or a closely related area. Demonstrated experience with 3D geometry and several relevant areas — multi-view reconstruction, SfM, SLAM, camera pose estimation, point-cloud registration, image-based localization, georeferencing, or sensor fusion. The ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems, choose the right mathematical or learning-based tools, and evaluate solutions rigorously. Strong Python skills and experience with modern ML and scientific-computing libraries (PyTorch, NumPy, SciPy). Strong software engineering skills — you can turn research prototypes into reliable, scalable, and maintainable systems. A track record of taking an algorithm from research idea and experimental prototype through evaluation, benchmarking, and deployment on real-world data. Clear written and verbal communication; able to collaborate effectively across research and engineering disciplines. Nice to Have PhD in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, photogrammetry, geodesy, remote sensing, or a related field — not required, but valued. A strong publication record or active involvement in the research community at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR, SIGGRAPH, 3DV, ICRA, or RSS. Experience with learning-based approaches for visual or 3D understanding — transformers, point transformers, foundation models, or methods combining learned representations with explicit geometric priors. Experience with aerial or satellite imagery, GNSS/GPS, geodesy, mapping systems, or large-scale spatial data. Evidence of technical leadership, mentorship, or successful cross-functional delivery. Compensation & Benefits Base salary: Competitive market rate. Compensation also includes an annual bonus, equity, and a comprehensive benefits package. title: Member of Scientific Staff, Cell Culture and Functional Assays
description: LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time The opportunity We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders. This role covers the cell side of our protein characterisation work. You would keep the cell lines healthy and run the assays that show how a designed protein behaves on a living cell, week after week, to the same standard. About us AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one. We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team. The role You will run cell culture and the cell-based assays for our protein characterisation work. That means the mammalian lines the assays depend on, from thaw through routine passage to a banked and documented stock, and the weekly rhythm of seeding, treating, reading and reporting plates. Most of it runs in 384-well plates with imaging-based or flow cytometry readouts. You will run those assays as designed, with the controls and replicates that make a curve defensible, and you will be the person who notices when a plate, a line or a reagent lot has started to drift. Assay design and the shape of the cascade sit with the scientist who leads this work today, so you are not being asked to invent the panel. You are being asked to make it run the same way every week, to record what you did in a form the rest of the system can read, and to tighten the protocols as they settle, including moving them towards the plate formats our automation will take on. Your first 90 days FIRST 30 DAYS ◆ Take over routine culture and banking for the protein cell lines, working to the protocols we already run. ◆ Learn the panel end to end by running each assay alongside the scientist who owns it. DAYS 30 TO 60 ◆ Run at least one assay in the panel independently, including its controls and acceptance criteria. ◆ Revise one culture or assay protocol so that someone else could follow it without asking you. DAYS 60 TO 90 ◆ Hold the weekly assay schedule on your own and return results on the agreed turnaround. ◆ Bring one protocol to a tighter precision bar, or into a plate format ready for automation. Who you are You are a hands-on cell biologist who takes assay variability personally. You have run the same assay often enough to tell a real effect from a bad plate, and you would rather find the cause than repeat the run. The week has a rhythm in this job: cells to feed, plates to seed, runs to finish, numbers to return. You are happy with that, you keep records someone else can pick up, and you say early when something looks wrong rather than at the end of the week. We do not hire people into boxes. The team is small, and early hires here end up owning work beyond the job they joined for. Nobody arrives with every part of this role. If you are strong in most of it and quick to learn the rest, we want to hear from you. MUST HAVE ◆ Strong hands-on mammalian cell culture: adherent and suspension lines, aseptic technique, and thawing, passaging and banking to a high and consistent standard. ◆ Experience running cell-based assays end to end, including relevant controls, replicates and dose-response curves behind a reported number. ◆ Comfort with plate-based work and the arithmetic that goes with it, such as dilution series, plate maps and normalisation. ◆ Careful, traceable record-keeping that someone else can follow without asking you. ◆ A PhD in cell biology, pharmacology, immunology or a related field, or an MSc and two to three years of relevant lab experience. NICE TO HAVE ◆ Reporter cell line bioassays for binding or blockade. ◆ Receptor internalisation, lysosomal trafficking or cytotoxicity assays. ◆ High-content or fluorescence imaging, and the image analysis behind it. ◆ 384-well formats, liquid handlers or other plate-based automation. ◆ Flow cytometry, for example for surface receptor quantification. Why this is unusual Most cell-based assay roles sit inside a discovery project. You build an assay, you answer a question with it, and the assay goes quiet. This one is closer to running an instrument. The same assays run every week against a stream of new molecules, and the number that comes out is the product. That changes what good looks like. Precision matters more than novelty, a protocol is only finished when someone else can run it and get your answer, and every passage, plate and reagent lot is captured as structured data, because a result is only as trustworthy as the cells behind it. Some people find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing in advance which one you are. How we work This is a lab-based role at our site in King's Cross, London. The cells are in the lab, so most of your week will be too, with room for writing and analysis away from the bench. The wider team is distributed and travels, so you will work with people who are not always in the building. We work in the open. Decisions are written down, work happens centrally rather than scattered across tools, and the week opens with a session the whole company attends. There is a quarterly offsite. Each person owns their area and makes the call inside it, and we will expect that of you early rather than late. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover. More is added as the team grows. The team you will join You will join the protein characterisation team and report to its lead. Day to day you will work with the scientist who designs the assay cascade, with the protein production and molecular characterisation scientists upstream of you, with the functional genomics team who share the cell culture suite, and with the engineers building the software and automation the lab runs on. We are a small, elite team, and this is the first seat given entirely to the cell-based side of the work. Our process Our process has four stages. A short screening call about the role and the practicalities. A behavioural interview about how you work, run from the same template for every candidate, before anything technical. A technical stage with the protein characterisation team, built around real work rather than a puzzle, including time with us in person at the lab. Then references, aimed at whatever we still want to understand. If you are not sure whether you match every line above, apply anyway. We would rather read it and decide. We are an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions on merit, scope-fit, and the strength of the working relationship we expect to build with each hire. Applications welcome from candidates of any background. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Member of Scientific Staff, Protein Production
description: LOCATION: King's Cross, London · PATTERN: Lab-based, full-time The opportunity We're a stealth startup in AI and bio, building infrastructure for data generation. The team is small and elite, the problems are hard, and the foundations are being laid right now. You'd help write them from the first line, with real ownership and a direct line to the founders. This role sits at the start of our protein work. Every measurement we make depends on the protein in the well being the right one, made the same way every time, and you would be one of the people making it. About us AI for biology has a data problem. The data that matters most doesn't exist yet, so we're building the infrastructure to produce it, with quality and traceability built in from day one. We're in stealth and heads-down on execution. We'll share more about what we're building once you've spoken with the team. The role You will make proteins, many of them at once. The work runs from DNA through to purified, quality-checked protein in 96-well format, ready for the binding and biophysical assays downstream of you. On the DNA side you will prepare expression templates from synthetic gene fragments, by PCR and by Golden Gate or Gibson assembly, and check them before they go forward. You will express proteins in cell-free systems first, with E. coli and mammalian (HEK293) expression following as the menu grows. You will purify them by affinity capture, mostly on magnetic beads in plates, and confirm what you made with quantification, CE-SDS and SEC. Every step is recorded as you go: what went in, which lot, which conditions, what came out, and what failed. Failed expressions and poor yields are kept as data, so they get the same care as the successes. As protocols settle you will help move them from the bench onto liquid handlers and our automated platform, working with the engineers who build it. This is a hands-on bench role, and in a small team you will also support the work either side of production when it needs doing. Downstream, that means molecular characterisation runs. Alongside, it means the cell culture behind our cell-based assays, from routine passage and banking to seeding assay plates. DAYS 60 TO 90 ◆ Run production week to week as part of the team, with QC results others can rely on without checking. ◆ Own and routinely execute a downstream characterisation readout, a mammalian expression route or maintenance of cell lines for a cell-based assay. Who you are You are a hands-on protein scientist who likes the bench and cares about doing the same thing well many times over. You have expressed and purified proteins yourself, you know what a failed prep looks like and why it failed, and you are comfortable working in plates rather than one tube at a time. You keep records someone else could follow without asking you. You say early when something is not working, and you are happy with a plan that changes as we learn. We do not hire people into boxes. advocate for fuel oil and feedstocks across product, sales, engineering and research teams Define and prioritise the Fuel Oil product roadmap with the product and technology teams Act as the primary subject matter expert for all Fuel Oil decisions across the business Building tools, models and AI agents (~25% of role) Design and build Sparta’s next generation of heavy products analytical tools quality Build scalable processes and delegate or automate routine tasks where it makes sense What we're looking for Required Deep Fuel Oil & Feedstocks market expertise — strong working knowledge of fuel oil benchmarks, differentials, blending economics, arbitrage mechanics, refinery economics, and global heavy products flows. At Sparta, our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, and high performance. We thrive in a fast-paced environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are embraced, and impact is rewarded. • Equity in a high-growth, VC-backed company • $42M in Series B funding — strong market traction and investment • Early-stage growth — build your career as we scale • Market-leading product — we are redefining commodity trading intelligence • Top-tier tools and technology to support your success What's the Culture Like at Sparta? At Sparta, our culture isn't just a set of values on a wall — it's how we work. We embrace a dynamic environment where initiative is celebrated, challenges are met head-on, and innovation thrives. You'll collaborate with people who are passionate about our mission and committed to building outstanding products and outcomes for our customers. The Sparta Code Understanding is non-negotiable Understanding leads to believing. Believing leads to winning. The 'why' is the difference between compliance and conviction. description: About Kyra Kyra is an enterprise influencer marketing platform working with brands like SharkNinja, Coach, H&M, Ray-Ban, and Converse. Our platform manages the full lifecycle — creator discovery, campaign management, content review, payments, analytics, and AI-powered intelligence across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube. 📍Europe (Remote) | 9-month Fixed-Term Contract 💰 Competitive, dependent on experience The Opportunity You will be the day-to-day owner of one of Kyra's largest and most complex global enterprise accounts: a fast-moving, multi-category consumer brand with 12+ sub-brands, 35+ active stakeholders, and campaigns running simultaneously across multiple regions. Your job is to keep delivery tight, keep the client happy, and be a safe pair of hands on a flagship account. This is not about growing or expanding the account. The commercial relationship is locked in. The job is world-class servicing at enterprise scale. What you'll do: Own the global account relationship across 12+ sub-brands and multiple regions. Stay organised across a volume of comms, briefs, and stakeholders that is genuinely unusual. Orchestrate cross-functional teams: creative, paid media, creator partnerships, and product. You are the connective tissue. If something drifts, you see it early and fix it. If something drifts (performance, scope, relationship, or timeline) you see it early and fix it. No surprises. Steady, organised ownership. 🎯 Lead the Relationship Own client relationships across product launches, seasonal campaigns, and always-on programmes. Multi-thread across their teams. Build trust at every level. Have direct conversations when performance needs to improve. 📈 Turn Insight into Strategy Translate campaign data into clear, executive-level recommendations using AI to move from raw numbers to narrative faster. Present performance against KPIs (engagement, EMV, sales lift, affiliate impact) and explain what it means. 🔍 Own Delivery End-to-End Lead client onboarding for new briefs: build decks, verify SOW accuracy, coordinate internal teams, demo the platform. With 6+ briefs running simultaneously, operational precision is everything. Make sure client feedback doesn't get lost. Feed client insights back into product development. Feed Insight Back into Product Surface client needs, pain points, and feature requests back into the product team. You are the closest person to how the client actually uses the platform. What We're Looking For We're looking for someone who has: 4–6+ years in influencer or creator marketing Campaign execution experience. You have actually run creative marketing activations, not just managed client relationships from a distance. Enterprise account servicing at scale. Multi-stakeholder, high-volume, complex. You have managed accounts with this many moving parts before. Exceptional organisation. The volume of comms, briefs, regions, and stakeholders on this account is unusually high. Getting lost is easy. You don't get lost. Self-starter with an entrepreneurial mindset. You take ownership of learning, build internal relationships proactively, and don't wait to be told what to do. Strong hands-on campaign experience, with real fluency in TikTok. AI fluency, applied. Our platform is AI-powered and you'll be expected to get up to speed fast and use it daily for client summaries, performance narratives, and campaign analysis. We're looking for people already comfortable using AI tools in their workflow, so the learning curve is the platform, not the concept. Comfortable working across project management tools (Asana, Airtable, Slack) and reporting dashboards. CPG or multi-category consumer brand experience is a plus. You should be commercially sharp, operationally reliable, and able to speak confidently about the accounts you've managed. Traits That Matter Proactive. Organised. Adaptable. Self-starting. Comfortable with ambiguity. You don't wait for problems to land. You see them coming and act. You don't need rigid processes or hand-holding. title: Software Engineer
description: About Singular Photonics Singular Photonics is a fast-growing fabless semiconductor start-up, developing Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) sensors that bring advanced computation directly into imaging. Our sensors enable innovations across LiDAR, fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM), spectroscopy and time-resolved optical measurements, powering next-generation solutions for customers worldwide. Based at Orchard Brae House in Edinburgh, we are a close-knit team at the forefront of the photonics revolution. About the Role We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to take a leading role in developing the Software Development Kit (SDK) for our SPAD sensors and cameras. You will build the interfaces that let customers configure our hardware, stream sensor data and turn single-photon measurements into results, supporting applications from early prototyping through to production. This role includes developing, documenting, and maintaining code for key sensor operations in various client languages. You will work closely with our hardware, firmware and applications engineers. Key Responsibilities SDK Development: Design, build and maintain the SDK and its client-language bindings Sensor Configuration: Implement functions to query and set up sensor configurations. Firmware Integration: Integrate and maintain communication with sensor firmware over Verilog, working alongside our firmware engineers. Data Management: Read, buffer and stream high-rate sensor data efficiently, keeping up with the throughput single-photon imaging generates. Data Processing: Develop algorithms for fluorescence lifetime, Raman spectra, diffuse correlation spectroscopy and time-of-flight data Visualisation & Signal Processing: Create tools for visualising sensor output and multi-dimensional data. API Integration: Expand SDK capabilities with partner APIs. Cross-Platform Development: Ensure compatibility across Windows and Linux. Cloud Integration: Enable cloud-based data processing and management. Quality, Testing & Documentation: Write the tests, documentation and release notes that go with production software, and help shape our development and release process as the team grows. Experience & Skills A minimum of three years’ experience designing and maintaining production software, including ownership of code through to release. Strong programming skills in [C++ or a comparable systems language], and comfortable moving between application-level and lower-level code. Experience working with hardware or sensor interfaces, and methodical debugging across the hardware and software boundary. Experience with Git and a collaborative development workflow including code review. Clear technical writing - you will be documenting an API that customers depend on. Comfortable in a small company where priorities shift and everyone pitches in. Experience building or maintaining an SDK, library or public API used by third parties. Experience with single-photon detection, TCSPC, LiDAR or time-of-flight systems desirable Signal processing, or algorithm work on high-rate or multi-dimensional data. Python binding frameworks GPU or parallel processing experience. Educational Background HNC/HND or undergraduate degree in Electronic Engineering, Computer Science, Physics, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience). Key Attributes & Behaviours Strategic thinker with a pragmatic, execution-focused mindset. Pragmatic judgement about when code is good enough to ship, and when it is not. Methodical debugger, comfortable when the problem could be in the software, the firmware or the hardware. Works well with all stakeholders who are not software specialists. Takes ownership end to end, from first design discussion to supporting a user Resilient and adaptable, and committed to high standards. Benefits of Joining Singular Photonics At Singular Photonics, we are committed to fostering a rewarding and supportive environment for our team. As a Software Engineer, you will benefit from: Pension: 5% company contribution. Share Options: Participation in the Company EMI Share Option Scheme, so you share in the growth you help build. Enhanced Annual Leave: 35 days paid annual leave per year, inclusive of UK public holidays. Hybrid Working: Primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week (full time worker). Career Growth: The opportunity to shape software development processes as the company scales. International Exposure: Work on technology with a growing international customer and partner base. Why Join Us This position offers a rare opportunity to own the software that customers use to get results from SPAD sensor technology. You will be a key member of a small, ambitious team, building something from the ground up and seeing the direct impact of your work as the company scales. Location & Work Environment Based at Orchard Brae House, Queensferry Road, Edinburgh. This is a full-time, permanent role, primarily office-based, with flexibility to work remotely up to two days per week. Right to work in the UK is essential. We are unfortunately unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Equal Opportunities Singular Photonics is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates and make appointments on merit, regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. If you need any adjustments to the application or interview process, please let us know and we will do what we can to accommodate you. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Director, Media Solutions - Scrum Master, UK
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong>About WPP Media</strong></p> <p>WPP is the trusted growth partner for the world’s leading brands. With exceptional talent, trusted data and intelligence, and world-class partnerships – all united by our pioneering agentic marketing platform, WPP Open – we help clients navigate change, capture opportunity, and deliver transformational growth. </p> <p>WPP Media is WPP's AI-driven media operating unit, bringing together media, data, and partnerships to deliver creative personalisation at scale. Connected through WPP Open and powered by Open Intelligence, clients see exactly where, how, and why their media investment is working.</p> <p>For more information, visit <a href="wppmedia.com">wppmedia.com</a>.</p></div><p><strong>3015 - Director, Media Solutions - Scrum Master, UK</strong></p> <p><strong>Role Summary and Impact</strong> </p> <p>You will work closely with teams across the United States, Europe, and Asia to deliver high-impact solutions in a collaborative, multicultural environment. We are seeking an experienced and passionate Scrum Master to guide and coach our development teams within Data & Technology Solutions. You will be a champion of Agile values and principles, fostering a culture of continuous improvement, transparency, and self-organization. Your role will be critical in enabling our teams to deliver high-quality data products and AI platforms efficiently and effectively, contributing directly to WPP's innovation in the AdTech space. </p> <p>You are: </p> <ul> <li>A leader who empowers teams, removing impediments and fostering an environment of collaboration and psychological safety. </li> <li>An expert facilitator, skilled at guiding teams through Agile ceremonies and discussions to achieve clear outcomes. </li> <li>A strong communicator and coach, adept at nurturing Agile mindsets and practices across individuals and the organization. </li> <li>Proactive and adaptable, able to anticipate challenges, resolve conflicts, and guide teams through change. </li> <li>Passionate about continuous improvement, always seeking ways to optimize team performance and delivery predictability. </li> </ul> <p>What you will do:</p> <p><strong>Facilitate Agile Processes and Ceremonies</strong> </p> <ul> <li>Facilitate all Scrum ceremonies (e.g., Daily Scrum, Sprint Planning, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective) ensuring they are productive, engaging, and aligned with Agile principles. </li> <li>Help the Product Owner manage the product backlog, ensuring stories are well-defined, estimated, and prioritized. </li> <li>Support the team in self-organizing and cross-functional collaboration, helping them to achieve sprint goals and ultimately, product vision. </li> <li>Ensure transparent communication of team progress, impediments, and metrics to all relevant stakeholders. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Coach and Develop Agile Teams</strong> </p> <ul> <li>Coach the development team on Scrum principles, Agile values, and engineering best practices to maximize productivity and continuous improvement. </li> <li>Provide guidance and support to the Product Owner in understanding and implementing Agile practices, particularly regarding backlog management and stakeholder collaboration. </li> <li>Foster a culture of open communication, inspect-and-adapt, and continuous learning within the team. </li> <li>Help resolve team conflicts and build a strong sense of team ownership and accountability. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Remove Impediments and Protect the Team </strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify, track, and actively work to remove impediments that hinder the team's progress and productivity. </li> <li>Shield the team from external distractions and interferences, allowing them to focus on sprint commitments. </li> <li>Collaborate with other Scrum Masters and management to identify and address organizational impediments to Agile adoption. </li> <li>Promote effective decision-making processes within the team, encouraging autonomy while ensuring alignment with broader goals. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Drive Continuous Improvement and Metrics </strong></p> <ul> <li>Guide the team in using metrics (e.g., velocity, burn-down/up charts) to understand and improve their performance and predictability. </li> <li>Lead retrospective meetings, facilitating discussions around "what went well," "what could be improved," and action items for the next sprint. </li> <li>Champion Agile adoption and maturity across the organization, sharing best practices and insights with other teams and leadership. </li> <li>Help the team establish and refine their definition of "Done" to ensure consistent quality and delivery. </li> </ul> <p><strong>Skills and Experience</strong> </p> <p>If this opportunity looks right for you, we are looking for candidates who have:  </p> <ul> <li>Experience as a dedicated Scrum Master for multiple software development teams, preferably in a data-intensive or technical product environment. </li> <li>Strong understanding and practical application of Scrum framework, Agile principles, and various Agile methodologies (Kanban, Lean). </li> <li>Proven ability to facilitate meetings effectively, manage conflict, and drive consensus. </li> <li>English fluency C1/C2 </li> <li>Excellent communication, coaching, and mentoring skills, with the ability to influence and inspire others. </li> <li>Experience with Agile project management tools (e.g., Jira, Azure DevOps, Asana). </li> <li>Understanding of the software development lifecycle and common engineering practices (e.g., CI/CD, TDD). </li> <li>Ability to understand complex technical issues at a high level and articulate them to non-technical stakeholders. </li> <li>Proactive problem-solver with a strong sense of ownership and accountability. </li> <li>Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Professional Scrum Master (PSM I/II), or other equivalent Agile certifications are highly desirable. </li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong></p> <p><strong>Life at WPP Media & Benefits</strong></p> <p>Our passion for shaping the next era of media is powered by our commitment to Be Extraordinary, investing in our employees to inspire transformational creativity. We also Lead Optimistically, firmly believing in and Championing Growth and Development for every individual. This commitment allows WPP Media employees to leverage the extensive global WPP Media & WPP networks to pursue their passions, build vital professional connections, and learn at the cutting edge of marketing and advertising. </p> <p>We Create an Open environment built on trust and respect, where everyone feels they belong and has opportunities to progress. This inclusive culture is fostered through a variety of employee resource groups and frequent in-office events showcasing team wins, sharing thought leadership, and celebrating holidays and milestone events. title: AI Transformation Strategist
description: Our Mission: Omnea is the agentic operating system for procurement. Procurement touches every pound a business spends, yet requests still stall for weeks and approvals get lost in inboxes. Our AI-first platform changes that: our agents capture requests, route approvals, onboard suppliers, flag risk and track every renewal, while anyone in the business can ask a question and get an answer grounded in their own company’s data. Buying becomes painless for everyone, procurement gets a seat at the table, and our customers have saved more than 100,000 hours of manual work so far. Companies like Spotify, PayPal, T. Rowe Price, JustEat, Adyen and S&P Global run procurement on Omnea. We’re backed by $75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners and Accel, and we’ve been named the UK’s number one startup in the Startups 100, ranked 11th on Sifted’s 2026 list of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, and recognised as one of Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies. Talent density matters more to us than almost anything else. We keep the bar high in every team, so everyone here has real ownership and real impact. Our team is full of former founders and operators who’ve scaled unicorns, and we’re looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside them. Find out more about the team and life at Omnea here . The Role As an AI Transformation Strategist, you'll work directly with our most strategic customers to understand their objectives and key challenges, identify high-impact AI opportunities, and translate them into measurable business value. You'll be building AI solutions on Omnea's procurement automation platform, combining the structured data flowing through requests, approvals, contracts, and supplier records with AI. Omnea gives AI the operational context of how a business actually buys, so it can move past answering questions and start taking action inside procurement itself: routing requests, flagging risk, drafting contract terms, negotiating with suppliers. There is no AI without that context. You'll prototype these solutions, demonstrate their value to executives, and ensure successful implementation, adoption, and value realisation, growing Omnea's footprint at those customers as you go. This customer-facing role is ideal for people who enjoy working directly with customers and turning complex business challenges into practical AI solutions. The focus is on problem framing, solution design, and business impact rather than pure implementation. While you will prototype AI solutions, the primary goal is to deliver meaningful business value to customers. What You'll Do Identify High-Impact AI Opportunities: Work closely with enterprise customers to understand their strategic priorities and operational challenges, identifying where AI can deliver measurable business value. Design AI-Powered Solutions: Translate complex business problems into scalable solution architectures, using Omnea's AI to eliminate manual work across procurement. Prototype and Demonstrate Value: Rapidly build prototypes and proof-of-value solutions that demonstrate tangible outcomes to business and technical stakeholders. Lead AI Innovation with Customers: Facilitate workshops, hackathons, and innovation sessions with customers to explore new ways AI can transform their operations. Drive Adoption and Business Impact: Partner with customer teams to ensure successful implementation, adoption, and realisation of measurable value from AI deployments. Develop Domain Expertise: Build deep expertise in specific industries or business domains (e.g., supply chain, finance) and help scale that knowledge across the organisation. What's Different About This Role You'll spend more time on problem framing and validation than on hand-building every proof of value. AI can generate a working prototype fast; your job is deciding whether it actually solves the customer's problem. Writing a sharp brief for what you want AI to build is now core to the role, not a side skill. Judgment on business impact matters more than raw build speed: which use case actually moves the metric the customer cares about, and which is just an impressive demo. You'll keep pushing on what's possible as Omnea's AI tooling evolves, and bring what you learn back to the rest of the team. About You You might be a great fit if you… 3+ years in transformation, strategy or operations work, ideally where AI or automation was part of the answer You take a messy business problem, form a hypothesis fast, and turn it into something that can actually be built You’re comfortable in front of a CFO or COO, whether that’s working through a problem on a whiteboard or presenting a formal readout You know how to measure the business impact of what you've delivered (pre- and post-delivery), and can turn that into a clear story for stakeholders - time saved, error rates down, adoption up, whatever the metric that actually matters to that customer You’d rather be accountable for the outcome than hand over the recommendation and move on Experience at a top-tier strategy consultancy is a big plus, though not required At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't quite match the full job spec! And regardless of your race, religion, colour, gender, or anything else! If you think you could be a good fit for Omnea, please reach out. A few things to note: We offer competitive geo-localised benefits, and you can check out our UK Benefits Package here and our US Benefits Package here . We work Tuesdays, Wednesdays & Thursdays in-person at our offices. At this early stage of our company life-cycle it's important to us that we get this together-time, and you can read more about why we believe this is a winning move here We're commercial, ambitious and we don't pretend otherwise! We're actively seeking folks looking to make the most of a career-defining opportunity, with the hunger to be part of building something really impressive . You can see our values here and our Omnea Future Founder's fund here ! We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background). We are proud to be recognised for both our culture and product, and we are just getting started. Join us as we grow! title: Head of FinOps
description: About Ryft Ryft is a regulated payment facilitator and authorised payment institution building the infrastructure layer for modern commerce platforms. We enable marketplaces, SaaS platforms and multi-party ecosystems to embed and monetise payments natively. Our technology handles onboarding, compliance, orchestration, split payments and revenue sharing, allowing our partners to focus on growth while we manage complexity. We are now entering the next phase of scale, expanding into new verticals and building a category-defining embedded payments platform. The role Every payment that goes through Ryft creates a trail of money moving between card schemes, acquiring banks, our accounts and our merchants. You make sure that trail adds up, every day, and that customer funds are protected exactly as the FCA requires. You'll own Ryft's financial operations end to end: reconciliations, settlement, safeguarding and the reporting that proves it. It's a hands-on role. You'll run the daily processes yourself, then automate them, so they scale as we launch in new markets and currencies. What you'll do • Reconciliations: run daily reconciliations across scheme and acquirer settlement reports, bank statements and our internal ledger. Investigate and resolve breaks quickly and accurately. • Safeguarding: own the daily internal and external safeguarding reconciliations under CASS 15, prepare the monthly safeguarding return, keep the resolution pack current and support the annual safeguarding audit. • Settlement and payouts: make sure merchants are paid the right amount on time, across currencies, and that split payments and escrow balances tie out. • Fees and cost of payments: reconcile interchange, scheme and acquirer fees against what we've billed, and flag where margin is leaking. • Disputes and chargebacks: track the financial side of chargebacks, refunds and reserves. • Month-end: feed accurate payment data into the close and work with Finance on revenue and balance sheet reconciliations. • Automation: work with Engineering and Product to replace spreadsheets with automated recs, alerts and dashboards. • Controls and documentation: write and maintain the SOPs, controls and evidence that auditors and the FCA will ask for., • Expansion: help design the finance operations for new payment flows, entities and licences, starting with our EU licence application in Malta. What we're looking for • 4+ years in financial operations, payment operations, treasury or reconciliations at a payments company, EMI, acquirer or fintech. • Hands-on experience of daily reconciliations at volume with the highest level of attention to detail. You know how to investigate and resolve the root cause of a break, not just clear it. • Working knowledge of UK safeguarding rules (PSRs 2017, EMRs 2011, CASS 15) and what an auditor expects to see. • You understand how card payments settle: schemes, acquirers, interchange and settlement cycles. • You'd rather build a process once than do it manually forever. • Comfortable taking full ownership of the end-to-end process, and liaising directly with Finance, Compliance, Engineering and our banking partners. Nice to have • Experience in a marketplace or platform payments business (split payments, escrow, payouts). • Multi-currency and FX settlement experience. • You've been through a safeguarding audit or a CASS 15 implementation. • Experience with reconciliation or safeguarding tools, or scripting (Python) to automate recs. • Exposure to setting up operations for a new entity or EU licence. description: At Moss, we give finance professionals the power to automate their day-to-day and make forward-thinking decisions. Join our Customer Success team, where you will focus on driving SaaS revenue growth through proactive customer engagement. While leveraging data insights, you will proactively identify upsell opportunities and mitigate churn risks. Your strategic guidance and deep product knowledge will be essential in helping customers unlock new value of our product and set them up for success. Your responsibilities Here's a bit more on what you can expect to be doing day-to-day: Drive customer engagement - through building and nurturing value-creating and scalable relationships, you develop a deep understanding of your clients’ and their finance goals. You guide and consult with them in order to drive their engagement and the activation of all the spend management features. Upsell - you leverage your deep understanding of both the product and your customer's needs to identify new business opportunities, as well as product and feature optimisation initiatives to increase value for existing accounts. Measure success and provide data insights - with the use of specific KPIs you aim to achieve and monitor revenue trajectory through, for example, key metrics such as spend engagement, SaaS uplift and renewals. Act as Product ambassador - working closely with internal stakeholders, you compile and communicate client feedback and act in an advisory capacity on current and future product features. Thrive for process excellence - you aim for continuous improvement, designing and delivering upon the client journey touchpoints that will increase customer satisfaction and contribute towards long-term retention. About you We think you’ll need the following experience and qualifications to succeed in the role: Proven experience in a proactive commercial-centric role, ideally in a B2B setting. Prior experience with upselling products and product features to existing clients. Fluent in English (C2).. In addition, here are the skills and attributes we are looking for: Customer obsessed - You empathize with the needs and pain points of the customer and provide a flawless experience. You have a structured way of working, employing efficiency and effectiveness in your day-to-day tasks. About Moss Moss is the Finance AI platform for Europe's mid-sized businesses, giving companies real-time visibility and full control over their spend. By automating card issuing, invoice management and expenses, Moss simplifies financial workflows and frees finance and accounting teams from manual, administrative work. Founded in Berlin and used by more than 10,000 businesses including Flink, Schufa, n8n and Auto1, Moss has raised €220+ million to date and operates in Germany, the Netherlands, the UK and further EU markets. Unless stated otherwise, benefits apply to full-time positions (interns and working students receive a tailored package). title: Lead Photonics Design Engineer - III/V Components
description: About us Salience Labs is developing optical circuit switching technology for AI infrastructure, aimed at reducing latency and cost in data centre networks. As we move towards deployment, you'll have real ownership of your area and work alongside a highly technical team on a hard problem in AI infrastructure. The role You'll join a multi-disciplinary research team in the UK to lead the development of III-V active components for integration with silicon photonics. You will take devices from epitaxial stack and device design through fabrication with external partners, to characterisation, reliability and qualification. What you'll be doing Lead the design and modelling of III-V active devices, including epitaxial layer structure, gain and power modelling, optical mode design, and electrical and thermal design Own the technology roadmap and device specifications for your area, translating system requirements into device design and integration targets Lead mask design and tape-outs, including GDS layouts, test structures and design-of-experiment splits Manage fabrication runs with external epitaxy and foundry partners: define process flows, review process and in-line data, and resolve yield issues as the technology scales Define and lead the characterisation strategy at wafer, chip and integrated-PIC level, including building and automating test setups Analyse test data, correlate measured performance with design and process variations, and drive design iterations to close performance gaps Work with packaging and reliability engineers on burn-in, accelerated ageing, failure analysis and qualification Mentor engineers and, as the team grows, help recruit and develop new team members Essential requirements PhD in physics, photonics, electrical engineering, optical engineering or a related subject with 6+ years' relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 8+ years' relevant experience, including at least 4 years' hands-on development of III-V optical amplifiers or semiconductor lasers, preferably in industry Proven track record of taking III-V devices from concept through design, fabrication and test, ideally including qualification Deep understanding of semiconductor laser and amplifier physics: optical gain, carrier dynamics, quantum-well design, noise, gain saturation and nonlinearities, thermal effects and polarisation dependence Hands-on knowledge of III-V epitaxy and fabrication processes (e.g. MOCVD/MBE growth, lithography, etching, passivation, metallisation, facet/AR coating), and experience working with external foundries Experience characterising amplifiers or lasers, including optical spectrum analysis, gain and noise measurement, wafer-level probing, temperature-controlled testing and test automation Experience with simulation and layout tools for photonic devices, such as Lumerical, Photon Design, Crosslight, RSoft, COMSOL, KLayout, L-Edit or Cadence Virtuoso Proven ability to lead technical projects across design, process, test and packaging functions, and experience mentoring or supervising engineers Excellent communication skills, critical thinking, attention to detail and self-motivation Nice to have Experience integrating III-V active devices with silicon photonics, including coupling design between III-V and silicon waveguides Experience line-managing a technical team Experience with reliability testing and failure analysis of III-V devices Experience developing PDK building blocks or compact models for active devices Programming experience (Python, MATLAB or C++) for simulation, test
